newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Friday as a rise in the new central bank fixing did not have much impact on the market, dealers said.
"The central bank raised the intervention and conversion rate by one point which prompted some foreign buying of the dollar," one European bank dealer said.
The dealer, however, said the foreign buying failed to have any impact on the market as local dealers preferred to stay on the sidelines.
The cental bank, Bank Indonesia, raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,323.00/2,515.00 and the conversion rate at 2,323.00/2,371 late on Friday.
Dealers said spot rupiah was last quoted at 2,323.60/24.00 against an opening of 2,324.00/24.50 on Friday.
Another foreign bank dealer said spot rupiah moved mostly in a narrow range due to a lack of fresh factors.
"The market remained slow most of the day as there are no fresh factors. The news on Lebed does not not have any impact on the market," the dealer said.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin's dismissal of security chief Alexander Lebed jolted major financial markets on Thursday.
Dealers said rupiah liquidity remained relatively adequate following the central bank's large injection of funds early on Friday.
Tom/next swap was last at 0.55/0.65 against an opening of 0.55/0.60. Overnight swap was last at 1.75/1.95 against an opening of 1.70/2.00.
One-month swap was quoted at 17.80/18.20, two at 35.00/36.0, three at 51.0/55.5 and six at 101.5/102.0 points.
